findings.summary: The default experience does not follow the system dark preference.
findings.evidence: The screenshot captured with prefers-color-scheme: dark remains a white, light-themed page, despite the CSS feature probe finding color-scheme rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the automatic theme the fresh-profile default, declare color-scheme: light dark, and ensure all page and community-content surfaces use preference-responsive tokens.

findings.summary: A language-variant prompt obscures core content on first load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a large prompt over the homepage/article before interaction. On mobile it occupies the bottom of an already scaled-down viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Move the preference choice to non-blocking chrome or defer it until the user opens language settings; if retained, provide reliable light-dismiss and avoid covering content.

findings.summary: The visible modal-like preference prompt is not exposed with a native dialog or popover primitive.
findings.evidence: The prompt is visible in screenshots, while the article DOM probe reports 0 dialog elements and 0 popover elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for a genuinely modal decision or popover for transient UI, with declarative invocation, focus management, Escape handling, and light-dismiss as appropriate.

findings.summary: The site forces a 1120 CSS-pixel desktop layout into a 360-pixel mobile viewport.
findings.evidence: The DOM reports meta viewport width=1120. The 360x800 layout records clientWidth 1120 and visual scale 0.321, and mobile screenshots show tiny desktop columns rather than reflowed content.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and reflow Vector/article layouts at narrow widths with intrinsic sizing, wrapping, and collapsible secondary chrome.

findings.guidanceId: touch target size hover fallback pointer input focus-visible
findings.summary: Touch targets and focus presentation are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports target-size failures. The focus probe found multiple visible buttons, links, and the search input with outline none and no compensating box shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 24 by 24 CSS-pixel targets with adequate spacing and a consistent high-contrast :focus-visible ring on every control.

findings.summary: The representative article loads too slowly under Lighthouse mobile conditions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse performance is 0.58 with FCP 4.2s, LCP 8.8s, Speed Index 5.3s, and TBT 210ms. The separate desktop trace was healthier at LCP 1.68s and TBT 24.81ms, showing a form-factor/network sensitivity.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the actual LCP resource, shorten critical request chains, and defer nonessential modules until after content and interaction readiness.

findings.summary: Critical delivery includes large scripts and render-blocking styles.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 54 requests and 1,055,413 transferred bytes. Scripts account for 635,308 bytes, including a 357,929-byte bundle, and three parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets are render-blocking candidates.
findings.suggestedFix: Split route-specific ResourceLoader modules, defer noncritical scripts, reduce initial stylesheet scope, and ensure only above-the-fold styles and scripts join the critical path.

findings.summary: The article ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 165 KiB unused JavaScript and 94 KiB unused CSS on the representative article.
findings.suggestedFix: Use ResourceLoader dependency data and coverage to split optional editor, discussion, popup, and gadget code from the reading path; conditionally load it when invoked.

findings.summary: Some images, controls, and links lack accessible alternatives or names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails image-alt, label, and link-name audits. The image probe reports 74 of 85 img elements without alt, including many content images, though some may be decorative.
findings.suggestedFix: Give meaningful images contextual alt text, use empty alt only for confirmed decoration, label every form control, and provide discernible text or accessible names for icon links.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not consistently visible across interactive chrome.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found several buttons, links, and inputs with computed outline none and no visible box-shadow. Lighthouse also reports unnamed links, weakening navigation context.
findings.suggestedFix: Centralise :focus-visible styling in Codex/Vector tokens, preserve it through component states, and verify a full keyboard traversal in reading order.

findings.summary: Public article pages omit a meta description.
findings.evidence: The article DOM probe reports description null and Lighthouse fails meta-description, although the title is descriptive.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate a concise, page-specific meta description from the lead section and keep it aligned with visible content.

findings.summary: Browser defenses are incomplete and the CSP remains broadly permissive.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence finds CSP with unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval, no frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, no response Referrer-Policy, and no Permissions-Policy. Cookie evidence finds a non-Secure zhwikimwuser-sessionId cookie and six SameSite=None cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Move toward nonce/hash-based CSP without unsafe-eval, add frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, and mark every state-bearing cookie Secure with the narrowest workable SameSite policy.

findings.summary: Article media is not consistently lazy-loaded, modern-formatted, or fully dimensioned.
findings.evidence: The image probe reports 73 below-fold images without loading=lazy, 79 legacy-format images, 3 missing dimensions, 5 missing srcset, and 2 oversized assets.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold media, preserve explicit dimensions, generate responsive srcset variants, and negotiate AVIF/WebP where source fidelity allows.

findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports missing source maps for large first-party JavaScript and Chrome inspector issues, lowering best-practices to 0.77.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish valid production source maps to authorized debugging channels and resolve the concrete Chrome Issues entries in the release pipeline.

findings.summary: Article and route changes use abrupt full-document swaps without View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The stylesheet probe found no view-transition usage across the representative article while navigation is a central repeated interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance eligible same-origin article navigation with cross-document View Transitions, while fully respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Long-form navigation chrome does not visibly adapt to scroll state.
findings.evidence: The long article screenshot and stylesheet probe show persistent table-of-contents/chrome but no scroll-state container query or scroll progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a progressively enhanced scroll-state query or lightweight progress affordance to keep location clear on very long articles without adding main-thread scroll handlers.
